evals.prompt: Draft a mutual NDA between Utopia Studio FZ-LLC (Dubai Internet City, Dubai, UAE; signatory Abdelrahman Mattar, Partner) and Nimbus Logistics Ltd (12 King Street, London, UK; signatory Sarah Patel, COO). We'll share pilot data, pricing and route-optimisation source code ahead of a paid pilot. Governing law England and Wales, 2-year term.
evals.expected_output: A complete mutual NDA naming both parties and signatories, covering pilot data, pricing and source code, with England and Wales governing law and a 2-year term, plain-language notes, and clauses needing legal review clearly flagged, plus a disclaimer that it is not legal advice.
assertions: Is mutual: both parties are bound as disclosing and receiving party
Names both companies, their addresses and the two signatories
Defines confidential information to include pilot data, pricing and source code
Sets governing law to England and Wales and a 2-year term
Includes standard exclusions (public, already known, independently developed, legally required disclosure)
Flags at least one clause for legal review and states it is not legal advice
Does not promise that injunctive relief or any remedy will be granted

evals.prompt: I'm a founder about to pitch my ed-tech idea to an individual angel investor next week. I want a short one-way NDA where only I disclose. My company is Qalam Labs (Riyadh, Saudi Arabia). The investor is a private person, Omar Haddad. Keep it to what's needed.
evals.expected_output: A one-way NDA with Qalam Labs as the only disclosing party and Omar Haddad as an individual receiving party, kept concise, with a note that many investors decline to sign NDAs and that Saudi law or another jurisdiction must be chosen and reviewed by counsel.
assertions: Is one-way: only Qalam Labs discloses and only Omar Haddad receives
Treats the receiving party as an individual, not a company
Is noticeably shorter than a full commercial NDA
Raises that the governing law and jurisdiction need to be chosen or confirmed (it was not specified)
Mentions that investors often decline to sign NDAs, or otherwise sets expectations about investor NDAs
Flags clauses for legal review and states it is not legal advice

evals.prompt: Make an NDA for a contractor developer we're hiring for 3 months to work on our app's payment integration. Our company is Fennec Pay Inc., Delaware. Contractor: Lina Mansour. Include return or destruction of materials when the contract ends.
evals.expected_output: An NDA suited to an individual contractor engagement, with Fennec Pay as discloser, covering technical and payment-related confidential information, a return-or-destruction clause at contract end, Delaware governing law suggested or asked about, flagged clauses, and a note that IP assignment belongs in the contractor agreement rather than the NDA.
assertions: Identifies Fennec Pay Inc. as the disclosing party and Lina Mansour as an individual contractor
Includes a clause requiring return or destruction of confidential materials when the engagement ends
Covers technical, source code or payment-system information specifically
Addresses governing law (Delaware or asks to confirm)
Notes that IP ownership or assignment should be handled in the contractor agreement, or flags it for review
Flags clauses for legal review and states it is not legal advice
